abstract_sources.abstract: Ensuring food safety requires rapid, sensitive, and portable detection methods to detect contaminants such as pesticides, heavy metals, antibiotics, and bacterial toxins. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as pivotal materials for constructing intelligent sensing platforms due to their tunable porosity, high surface area, and versatile functionalization. This review systematically explores recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-driven MOF design, highlighting structural engineering strategies to increase the stability, sensitivity, and selectivity. Innovations in fluorescence, colorimetric, electrochemical, and surface-enhanced raman spectroscopy (SERS) sensors have demonstrated the multifunctionality of MOFs in complex food matrices. Integrated sensing platforms with smartphones, microfluidic chips, and nanozyme technologies enable real-time, onsite detection with enhanced efficiency. Challenges such as multiplex detection, material stability, and applicability to real samples are critically discussed. Future directions emphasize machine learning-assisted signal optimization, standardized protocols, and the development of multimodal platforms for food safety monitoring. This review provides valuable guidelines for advancing MOF-based intelligent systems from structural innovation to practical deployment.

abstract_sources.abstract: The review examines molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) technology and its potential applications to present current scientific progress in the field. It highlights that MIPs production at an industrial scale faces difficulties because different types of intermolecular interactions and polymerization conditions and material performance create complex synthesis challenges. Emphasis is placed on the versatility of MIPs in environmental monitoring, the food industry, extraction, sensors, drug delivery, and biomedicine, with the discussion on the integration of MIPs pointing out the possibilities for enhancing accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, combining MIPs with analytical and computational methods creates new opportunities for qualitative and quantitative evaluation. In this light, the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve MIP performance, expedite polymerization procedures, and forecast ideal monomer-template interactions is expanding. This manuscript offers a fresh viewpoint using combined MIP applications in biosensing, drug delivery, environmental treatment, food safety, and catalysis with AI-driven strategies. It also aims to establish a framework for the future development of the next generation of smart and sustainable technologies.

abstract_sources.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are a cutting-edge class of coordination materials distinguished by their high porosity, structural diversity, and multifunctionality, enabling their rapid expansion across biomedicine, food science, biotechnology, and energy-related applications. The current review starts with a brief overview of MOFs classification together with overview of conventional physical and chemical synthesis as well as emerging green approaches. Specific attention is retained on green routes that employ benign solvents, energy efficient conditions and sustainable precursors to minimize environment impact. Next recent progress in MOFs applications is critically discussed covering biomedical, biotechnology/food related fields and energy applications. Key application areas include drug delivery, bioimaging, wound healing, biocatalysis, food packaging, fruits/vegetable ripening, electrochemical water splitting such as hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions (HER and OER). The current review emphasizes growth towards transition from new laboratory-scale discoveries to applications-oriented systems with practical relevance. Despite substantial achievements, large-scale deployment of MOFs remains constrained due to several challenges including limited reproducibility at the industrial level, inadequate stability under operational conditions, environmental concerns associated with synthesis and disposal, and cost constraints. To address these barriers, the present review examines emerging multiscale strategies ranging from molecular design to process engineering. In particular, the growing/emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in predicting MOFs properties, structures, and synthetic routes is critically argued as a transformative tool for accelerating realistic design and scalable production. Overall, the review aims to offer a forward-looking perspective on the sustainable development of MOFs, emphasizing scalable synthesis, data-driven design and green chemistry principle to transfer fundamental research to real-world applications needed for resource preservation and sustainable development.

abstract_sources.abstract: Batteries are currently the most widely utilized electrochemical energy storage devices. The properties of the electrode/electrolyte interface, which serves as the critical region for electrochemical reactions and charge transfer, significantly determine the performance of lithium-ion batteries. Therefore, precise characterization and analysis of the electrode/electrolyte interface are crucial for the development of high-performance lithium-ion batteries. In contrast to traditional ex situ characterization methods, in situ characterization techniques can monitor the evolution of material or device properties in real-time under actual operating conditions, thereby avoiding potential interference and contamination during sample preparation and transfer. This capability renders in situ techniques an essential research tool in battery development. This review systematically summarizes the in-situ characterization techniques employed in recent studies concerning the evolution of electrode/electrolyte interfaces from three perspectives: morphology, composition, and physicochemical properties. It highlights the latest application scenarios for each testing method while emphasizing their respective advantages and disadvantages. Furthermore, the review discusses the application of artificial intelligence technology in image processing, data mining, and inference, and anticipates future trends in testing and data analysis technologies.

abstract_sources.abstract: Uranium extraction from seawater and uranium-containing wastewater represents a critical challenge for sustainable nuclear energy development. Photocatalysis has emerged as a promising green strategy due to its high efficiency, environmental compatibility, and potential for solar-driven operation. Among diverse photocatalysts, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have shown exceptional potential owing to their tunable porosity, rich active sites, and adjustable electronic structures. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in MOF- and COF-based photocatalytic uranium extraction, emphasizing structure–activity relationships and strategies to enhance light absorption, charge separation, and stability. Particular attention is devoted to the integration of data-driven methods, especially machine learning (ML), to accelerate material discovery and performance prediction. The Random Forest algorithm is introduced as a representative approach for correlating structural descriptors—such as surface area, pore size, and band gap—with uranium removal efficiency. By bridging experimental data and predictive modeling, ML-guided photocatalysis offers a paradigm shift toward rational design of high-performance materials. Finally, the review highlights current challenges and future perspectives for developing intelligent, sustainable, and scalable photocatalytic systems for uranium recovery from complex aqueous environments.

abstract_sources.abstract: The need for hydrogen (H_{2}) storage arises from the increasing interest in H_{2} as an eco-friendly and facile energy carrier for multiple applications, including energy storage devices, transportation and industrial processes. H_{2} emerges as a promising and sustainable alternative to conventional fossil fuels because of its high energy density and potential for generating zero-emission energy when utilized in fuel cells. Moreover, global carbon dioxide (CO_{2}) emissions have remained a significant concern to mankind. The combustion of fossil fuels, industrial processes, deforestation and land-use changes have been major contributors to CO_{2} emissions. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are suitable candidates for addressing the challenges related to the transportation, distribution and utilization of H_{2} and capturing CO_{2} to contribute to lowering the carbon footprint. This review article highlights the challenges, strategies and recent progress in H_{2} storage and carbon capture using mostly mixed ligand MOFs. It focuses on three key strategies for constructing effective MOF adsorbents, such as optimizing framework structure and porosity and modifying functional groups. It also discusses a few representative examples and emphasizes material design strategies and the structure-property relationship. Furthermore, the discussion highlights how researchers can overcome conventional barriers in material design and discovery by utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to accelerate the development of next-generation MOF-based gas storage systems in a more time- and cost-efficient way.

abstract_sources.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) catalysts offer compositionally tunable surfaces containing diverse local atomic ensembles, making them promising platforms for electrocatalytic reactions such as HER, OER, ORR, NRR, CORR/CO_{2}RR, HOR, NO_{3}RR and NORR. However, their vast compositional space, surface segregation, dynamic reconstruction, and site-dependent adsorption behavior make conventional trial and error screening and exhaustive DFT calculations inefficient. This review critically discusses how machine learning can accelerate HEA catalyst discovery by linking composition, local structure, adsorption energetics, catalytic activity and stability. Particular attention is given to HEA-specific descriptors, reaction-dependent activity indicators, DFT- and experiment-derived datasets, graph neural networks, uncertainty quantification, model interpretability, transferability, and active learning strategies. We further outline closed-loop workflows that combine automated HEAs prediction, high-throughput characterization, electrochemical testing, model retraining, and experimental feedback. Finally, key challenges are identified, including the lack of standardized catalytic datasets, limited representation of reconstructed surfaces, insufficient negative data, and weak transferability across reactions. These challenges define the next stage of ML-enabled HEA catalyst design, where predictive models must be directly connected to experimentally validated electrocatalytic performance.

abstract_sources.abstract: The ever-increasing global demand for lithium, fueled by the paradigm shift toward renewable energy storage, has led to the need for the development of more sustainable and efficient extraction technologies. Conventional lithium extraction methods—primarily solar evaporation—are increasingly scrutinized due to their protracted processing timelines, significant environmental footprint, and low selectivity. This review provides a comprehensive critical analysis of photothermal-driven interfacial evaporation as a transformative, low-energy strategy for lithium-ion separation, focusing on latest advances from 2020 to 2026. We begin by benchmarking interfacial solar evaporation against traditional extraction frameworks, highlighting its superior energy efficiency and localized thermal management. Furthermore, the fundamental coordination characteristics of Li^{+} and its role in the extraction mechanism as well as coordination site matching functional materials in complex brine systems are outlined. A rigorous exploration of the mechanistic pathways follows, focusing on the interplay between localized photothermal heating and ion kinetic transport at the liquid-vapor interface. Furthermore, we survey the state-of-the-art in photothermal materials and device designs, including their ability to maintain high evaporation rates while facilitating selective ion permeation. Finally, the review addresses the critical challenges of upscaling and limited selectivity, proposing a forward-looking perspective on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for the accelerated discovery and optimization of next-generation photothermal materials.

abstract_sources.abstract: Escalating ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure, the prevalence of skin disorders, material deterioration, and environmental concerns associated with conventional UV filters have heightened the need for efficient next-generation UV-shielding materials. This review offers a comprehensive and progressive overview of effective UV-shielding systems, connecting fundamental photophysical mechanisms with emerging multifunctional material designs. Emphasis is placed on inorganic metal oxide nanostructures, naturally derived biopolymers, and their advanced hybrid nanocomposites highlighting their UV-shielding mechanisms, structure-property relationships, synthesis approaches, and stability. Their applications in food packaging, dermatology, smart textiles, wearable electronics, and intelligent coatings are thoroughly assessed regarding practical performance and industrial significance. This study goes beyond material design to examine life cycle sustainability, regulatory constraints, and commercialization obstacles that are insufficiently addressed in existing literature. Furthermore, rising artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and autonomous materials discovery methodologies are emphasized as pivotal instruments for expediting the design and enhancement of UV-shielding systems.

abstract_sources.abstract: Metal phthalocyanines (MPcs) have emerged as promising redox-active materials for next-generation electrochemical energy storage owing to their tunable electronic structures, reversible multi-electron redox behavior, high chemical stability, and versatile coordination chemistry. This review critically summarizes recent advances in MPc-based electrode materials for rechargeable batteries and supercapacitors during 2022–2026, with particular emphasis on structure-property relationships, molecular engineering strategies, electrochemical mechanisms, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted materials design. Recent studies demonstrate that hybridization of MPcs with conductive carbon materials, conductive polymers, and metal–organic frameworks significantly enhances electrical conductivity, ion transport, and electrochemically active surface area, leading to remarkable improvements in electrochemical performance. Representative MPc-based electrodes have achieved reversible capacities exceeding 1080 mAhg^{−1} in lithium-ion batteries, specific capacitances up to 824 Fg^{−1} in supercapacitors, energy densities of 86.2 Whkg^{−1}, and cycling stability of up to 100,000 charge–discharge cycles, highlighting their considerable potential for high-performance energy-storage applications. Furthermore, density functional theory, molecular dynamics simulations, and operando characterization have provided valuable insights into charge-storage mechanisms and redox processes, while AI and machine learning are emerging as powerful tools for accelerating molecular design and performance optimization. Despite these advances, challenges associated with intrinsic electrical conductivity, molecular aggregation, electrolyte compatibility, and scalable device fabrication remain.

abstract_sources.abstract: Oil-water pollution poses a significant environmental threat due to frequent oil spills and industrial discharges, which severely impact aquatic ecosystems and human health. Conventional separation methods, such as gravity separation, centrifugation, and chemical coagulation, often incur high operational costs, generate secondary pollution, and exhibit low reusability, necessitating sustainable alternatives. Chitosan, a biodegradable and renewable biopolymer derived from chitin, has emerged as an effective adsorbent owing to its abundant amino and hydroxyl groups and tunable surface chemistry. However, Chitosan magnetic nanocomposites (CMNCs) comprise magnetic nanoparticles functionalized with chitosan, thereby enhancing separation efficiency, recoverability, and recyclability. This review systematically discusses the structural and physicochemical fundamentals of chitosan and magnetic nanoparticles, along with various synthesis routes, such as in situ co-precipitation, solvothermal, and green synthesis methods. Surface wettability, electrostatic interactions, and hydrogen-bonding interactions elucidate the mechanisms of oil-water separation. Furthermore, this review also elucidates the roles of magnetic recovery and fluid dynamics, including particle image velocimetry (PIV) analysis. The review also explores the physicochemical and adsorption properties of magnetic chitosan composites across various separation techniques, including filtration and coagulation, and highlights their regeneration and recyclability. Post-spectroscopic analysis further elucidates the structural integrity, surface topology, and bonding interactions. Besides, advanced computational methods, such as Density Functional Theory (DFT), Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, and emerging Machine Learning (ML) approaches, are discussed to understand interfacial interactions, optimize adsorbent design, and predict separation performance. Overall, this comprehensive review highlights the potential of CMNCs as reconfigurable materials for sustainable oil-water separation and environmental remediation.
